title: Alternative routes

blocks.heading: Alternative routes
blocks.text: Non-formal courses, vocational education and lifelong learning can provide different routes to skills and continued participation. Their development contribution depends on relevance, access and opportunities to use learning. A certificate alone cannot create demand for a skill.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Vocational education
blocks.text: Vocational education develops practical knowledge and skills relevant to particular occupations or work activities. It can fit a documented skill gap when tools, training quality and work opportunities align; a narrow course with no usable equipment or demand offers weaker evidence of benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Lifelong learning
blocks.text: Lifelong learning continues across life through different formal, non-formal and informal opportunities. It can help people adapt to change but needs time, access and support. Adult responsibilities should inform the arrangement rather than be treated as lack of motivation.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: A fictional tailoring course has trained instructors, appropriate machines and local employers willing to assess applicants. Practical work can develop useful skills, while classroom explanations help learners understand methods. Employment still depends on opportunities and the quality and recognition of the training. A vocational label alone does not guarantee either competence or a job.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
